newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa to host government-rebel talks on Zaire.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa to host government-rebel talks on Zaire.

text.p: Zaire's government and rebels will meet in South Africa for talks this week, maybe as soon as Thursday, President Nelson Mandela said on Wednesday.
"Representatives of the contesting parties have made a request that they would like to meet in South Africa...to be able to discuss their problems," Mandela told reporters.
He said he had agreed to host their talks.
Mandela was speaking after talks in Cape Town with regional leaders on how to defuse the growing conflict in Zaire and quell unrest in southern Africa's tiny Swaziland and Lesotho.
He said South Africa would send air transport to pick up Zaire's rebel leader from Kigali in Rwanda -- but he did not mention Laurent Kabila, the mastermind behind the uprising, by name.
He said he hoped the talks could begin on Thursday.
Fighting in Zaire has intensified, with ailing President Mobutu Sese Seko's government launching air strikes this week on rebels who have seized much of the east of the country since October.
Zaire says rebels are backed by troops from neighbouring Rwanda, Uganda and Burundi, which deny involvement.

South African officials had said Mandela, seen by many Africans as their continent's greatest hope for peace, sought a political response to the problem. "The idea of military intervention is very much on the back burner," one said.
